title: OpenAI fn-bridge: deterministic tool selection and message framing for function/function-call compatibility
author: Maya Hernandez
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: deterministic mapping and selection between OpenAI function_call and Redwood tool semantics.
Streaming stability: partial tool messages now emitted as preserved tool-stream frames and reassembled on the client side.
SDKs (Python/TS) updated to expose ToolChoice vs legacy FunctionCall objects; minimal migration guidance included.
description: Context: Customers using OpenAI-style function/tool calling reported subtle differences in how models return function_call vs tool_choice outputs. This PR introduces the 'fn-bridge' layer that normalizes incoming OpenAI responses into Redwood's tool model, clarifies tool_choice semantics, and stabilizes streaming of tool messages. Summary of changes: 1) fn-bridge mapping: robust translation from OpenAI function schemas to Redwood tool schemas, including support for nested object params, optional fields, and x-openai legacy hints. 2) Deterministic selection: when the model returns both a top-level function_call and a tool_choice (or multiple tool choices), the bridge uses a deterministic selection policy: prefer explicit tool_choice when present; otherwise use function_call name; tie-breaker uses score > confidence_threshold or deterministic lexicographic order to avoid non-deterministic flip-flops in canary/rollouts. 3) Streaming behavior: streaming tokens that belong to tool output are now emitted as incremental 'tool_message_patch' frames with metadata (tool_name, seq, partial=true). The final aggregated payload is published as a single 'tool_message' event once the stream completes. This change prevents corrupted JSON when clients reassemble partial tool outputs. 4) Backwards compatibility: models/clients that only emit function_call still work. We added an opt-in mapping flag for legacy tool schemas and a compatibility shim for older SDK clients. 5) SDK updates: Python and TypeScript SDKs now expose ToolChoice objects (tool_name, reason, score, messageFragments) and a unified call() surface that accepts both 'functions' and 'tools' parameter forms. 6) Tests and CI: comprehensive unit/integration tests added; new e2e streaming test that asserts reassembly and no token loss; perf canary run shows no regression in 95th percentile latency under typical workloads. Migration notes: No breaking changes for most users. If you provide custom tool schemas, add an explicit mapping for ambiguous signatures or enable 'fn_bridge.legacy_mapping=true' in the service config to maintain old behavior. For SDK consumers, update to the latest SDK to receive ToolChoice objects; older SDKs will continue to receive a legacy FunctionCall-style payload but are not guaranteed to get incremental tool_message_patch frames. Why this is needed: prior behavior produced ambiguous events when a model returned both function_call and tool_choice or when streaming cut JSON fragments across packets. This produced client-side parsing errors and nondeterministic tool selection during rollouts. This PR eliminates those sources of instability and provides a clear compatibility pathway. The remainder of the PR lists commits, files changed, review convo, CI summary, and merge details below.

review_comments: Nik Patel: Please clarify the tie-breaker behavior when two tools have equal score; suggestion to use deterministic ordering instead of random selection.
Maya Hernandez: Updated implementation to use deterministic lexicographic ordering as tie-breaker and added unit tests that assert repeatable selection across runs.
Sofia Ramos: Can we avoid emitting tool message patches for very small payloads to reduce overhead? Could be a perf regression.
Maya Hernandez: Added heuristic to send final tool_message immediately if total bytes < 256 to avoid extra patch frames; tested in perf canary.
Arun Gupta: SDK changes look good; ensure older clients receive a clear compatibility header so they know payload shape changed.
